decision.explanation: Using the angle-addition identity, sin(x+150°)=sin(x)cos(150°)+cos(x)sin(150°). Since cos(150°)=-√3/2 and sin(150°)=1/2, the result is (cos(x)-√3 sin(x))/2.

after.name: Question 1
after.worked_solution:
Recall the sum formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(u+v)=\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v+\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v
$$

Applying the sum formula for sine with $u=x$ and $v={150}^{∘},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+{150}^{∘}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡{150}^{∘}+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡{150}^{∘} \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot (-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2})+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot (\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{2}+\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x-\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Simplifying Expressions in Degrees Using the Sum and Difference Formulas
content.worked_solution:
Recall the sum formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(u+v)=\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v+\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v
$$

Applying the sum formula for sine with $u=x$ and $v={150}^{∘},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+{150}^{∘}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡{150}^{∘}+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡{150}^{∘} \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot (-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2})+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot (\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{2}+\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x-\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
